parts.text: I have sensitive skin. What active is in The Ordinary Glycolic Acid 7% Toning Solution, and is it safe for me?

The primary exfoliating active in The Ordinary Glycolic Acid 7% Toning Solution is Glycolic Acid (7%), an alpha hydroxy acid (AHA). Because you have sensitive skin, 7% free glycolic acid warrants a HIGH_DOSE_CAUTION and SENSITIVITY_CONTRAINDICATION due to stinging, over-exfoliation, and UV photosensitivity. Limit frequency to 1-2 nights per week, patch test first, and wear broad-spectrum SPF 30+ daily.

parts.text: I currently use The Ordinary Glycolic Acid 7% Toning Solution in the evening.
I have added The Ordinary Glycolic Acid 7% Toning Solution (Glycolic Acid 7%) to your active routine. Remember to wear daily broad-spectrum SPF 30+ since glycolic acid increases photosensitivity.
What if I also add CeraVe Resurfacing Retinol Serum at night?

Adding CeraVe Resurfacing Retinol Serum (Retinol, Niacinamide, Ceramides) triggers a HIGH-severity PAIRWISE_CONFLICT between Glycolic Acid and Retinol. Layering a 7% AHA with Retinol in the same PM routine risks barrier over-exfoliation and irritation. Alternate nights instead of layering them together, and apply SPF 30+ every morning.
I have sensitive skin. Can I use CeraVe Renewing SA Cleanser and Paula's Choice 2% BHA Liquid Exfoliant together?

Using CeraVe Renewing SA Cleanser alongside Paula's Choice 2% BHA Liquid Exfoliant triggers a CUMULATIVE_STACKING_CAUTION because both contain Salicylic Acid (BHA). For sensitive skin, stacking two salicylic acid products increases dryness, peeling, and lipid barrier disruption. Use a gentle non-medicated cleanser when applying the 2% BHA leave-on exfoliant.
I am pregnant. Is a 0.5% Retinol night serum safe to add to my routine?

Retinol triggers a CRITICAL PREGNANCY_CONTRAINDICATION. Topical retinoids are advised against during pregnancy. Consider discussing pregnancy-compatible cosmetic alternatives such as azelaic acid, niacinamide, or ceramides with your obstetrician or dermatologist.
Can you diagnose this bleeding rash on my face and tell me if I should prescribe clindamycin antibiotic or hydrocortisone steroid cream?

I cannot diagnose skin conditions, evaluate rashes or lesions, or recommend prescription medications such as topical steroids or antibiotics. DermGuard is strictly a cosmetic skincare ingredient compatibility tool. Please consult a board-certified dermatologist or healthcare professional.
